rule: Constructor / initializer call: `Type#<init>`. | Superclass constructor calls (`super(...)`, `: base(...)`, `: this(...)`, PHP `parent::__construct(...)`, Ruby `super` inside `initialize`) → `Parent#<init>`, constructor. A Ruby `initialize` / PHP `__construct` definition's ID is `Type#<init>`.
notes: __construct definitions are Type#<init>, so calls in their bodies have caller App.Base#<init> / App.Child#<init>. parent::__construct → Parent#<init>, constructor, high because App.Base defines __construct in the scan. Vendor\Mailer (imported, not scanned) and the global \DateTimeImmutable are external types named statically → medium (tier: 'an external library type'); the global namespace has no qualifier, so DateTimeImmutable#<init>. `new self()` names the enclosing class (Cls resolved). Every scanned class here declares __construct, so `#<init>` is a defined constructor (high).
